reader.summary: The week was dominated by Kim Jong Un's unannounced visit to China, where he crossed a newly inaugurated cross-border bridge into Dandong, signaling a noticeable warming of trade and diplomatic ties with Beijing. The trip reinforced a broader pattern of North Korea deepening its alliance with both China and Russia. Simultaneously, tensions with the South escalated sharply: Pyongyang ordered border troops to take 'resolute action' if Seoul threatened their safety, and Kim Yo Jong warned that anti-South propaganda loudspeakers would be operational within days. South Korea responded by proposing military talks to calm the border and vowing 'resolute punishment' if new measures were deployed. Kim also called for a 'military revolution' to strengthen army units. A separate thread saw North Korean websites suffer a DDoS cyberattack and intermittent outages, raising questions about the regime's digital defenses. Recurring rumors of Kim's death or coma prompted an official Pyongyang response, while a new report described North Korean workers at a Russian drone factory as being treated like 'slaves.' Trump downplayed talk of a possible meeting with Kim next month. Overall, the week showed a North Korea simultaneously courting its eastern partners while posturing aggressively toward the South.

display.tldr: North Korea will switch on its border loudspeakers and South Korea will respond with a formal military statement. The China alliance will deepen through follow-up diplomatic announcements. A new military exercise will follow Kim's revolution call.
display.eli5:
North Korea and South Korea are arguing across their shared border. Pyongyang just told its soldiers to be ready to act if Seoul threatens them, and it says it will turn on loudspeakers that blast propaganda toward the South within days. South Korea has proposed talks to calm things down, but also promised a strong response if new weapons show up.

The reason this is happening is that both sides are trying to look tough. North Korea just visited China and is feeling confident about its alliances, so it is doubling down on its posture toward the South. At the same time, Kim Jong Un has ordered his army to go through a military revolution, which means new drills and equipment are coming.

Next week, expect the border loudspeakers to actually go live and South Korea to issue a formal response. You will also probably see a new military exercise or parade in North Korea, and some follow-up diplomatic talk between Pyongyang and Beijing.

The surprise would be if Trump and Kim suddenly announce they are actually meeting. He downplayed it this week, but the back channel is still open, and a sudden summit would change everything about how the other countries react.
